headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: Claude Code can read/write shared files and egress broadly, while Chatwoot handles customer data and integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read repo/user directories and use MCP, so if Chatwoot exports support content into shared files or an MCP bridge, prompt injection is plausible. Chatwoot’s integrations and customer-facing messages increase the chance of attacker-controlled text entering the workflow. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into files or MCP inputs that Claude Code reads
IF an attacker can place instructions in customer messages or support artifacts
mitigations: Disable automatic file handoff between systems
Strip instructions from imported support text
Use a read-only export format for Chatwoot artifacts
Review MCP server inputs before enabling them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while Claude Code can read files, run shells, and egress broadly. If Chatwoot data is placed in shared files or the terminal workspace, Claude Code can transmit it off-host. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF customer records or interaction logs are present in Claude Code's workspace
IF Claude Code is allowed to send workspace contents to external services
mitigations: Keep customer data out of the coding workspace
Use a separate redacted export for debugging
Restrict network egress during support-data handling
Rotate any secrets found in shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Chatwoot is a customer-support system that may also operate on shared files or exported artifacts. If both touch the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git changes can corrupt state or overwrite work. The shared-state path is explicit for Claude Code, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports artifacts into the same directory Claude Code edits
IF Claude Code and Chatwoot both modify the same git working tree
mitigations: Use separate directories for support exports and code work
Pause Claude Code before Chatwoot writes shared artifacts
Commit or stash git changes before cross-tool handoff
Limit Claude Code to read-only mode on shared repos
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and git state, so if it consumes Chatwoot-generated reports or summaries as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate into code or operational changes. Chatwoot can produce customer-facing reports, but no direct automation link is documented. The pathway exists, yet verification can be added, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Claude Code treats Chatwoot reports as ground truth
IF those reports are used to drive commits, scripts, or shell actions
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Chatwoot outputs
Mark imported summaries as untrusted
Cross-check key facts against source records
Use a checklist before any commit or shell action
requires-engineering: add validation gates between tools

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Claude Code runs locally but sends requests to api.anthropic.com and handles API keys and git credentials. If regulated customer data is placed into Claude Code’s context, residency or retention obligations may diverge from Chatwoot’s support workflow. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied into Claude Code prompts or files
IF the organization requires residency or retention controls not met by external API processing
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Claude Code context
Redact customer identifiers before transfer
Confirm retention terms for the external API
Separate support records from coding workspaces
requires-engineering: document a data-flow and residency review
